facts.statement: Fossils of Pterodromoides were first found at the Punta Nati site on the island of Menorca in the western Mediterranean.
facts.quote: Its fossil remains were first discovered at the Punta Nati palaeontological site on the island of Menorca in the Balearic archipelago of the western Mediterranean.

facts.statement: A specimen found in North Carolina suggests the species lived across the North Atlantic.
facts.quote: An additional specimen from North Carolina, USA has also been referred to this species, suggesting it lived across the North Atlantic.

facts.statement: Fossils were excavated from Punta Nati, Menorca, in August 1995 by Josep Quintana and Salvador Moyà-Solà.
facts.quote: The fossilized remains of Pterodromoides were found in blocks of sediment excavated from Punta Nati, Menorca in August 1995 by Josep Quintana and Salvador Moyà-Solà.

facts.statement: The species was named Pterodromoides minoricensis in 2001 based on a skull and postcranial remains.
facts.quote: A small sample of these, including a skull and some postcranial remains, were recognized to represent a new genus and species, which was named Pterodromoides minoricensis in 2001.

facts.statement: The holotype for the species is a cranium designated as IPS 11826.
facts.quote: A cranium (IPS 11826) was designated as the holotype of this species.

facts.statement: A partial left humerus found at the Yorktown Formation in North Carolina has been assigned to this species.
facts.quote: In addition, a partial left humerus (USNM 464315) found in the deposits of the Yorktown Formation at Lee Creek Mine, North Carolina, has been referred to P. minoricensis.

facts.statement: The genus lived during the Late Miocene epoch.
facts.quote: Pterodromoides is an extinct genus of fulmarine petrel dating from the Late Miocene.

facts.statement: The species lived between 5.333 and 2.58 million years ago during the Zanclean to Piacenzian ages.
facts.quote: Time range: Zanclean to Piacenzian (5.333 to 2.58 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus contains only one known species, P. minoricensis.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, P. minoricensis.

facts.statement: It was a medium-sized bird similar in shape and proportions to modern petrels of the genus Pterodroma.
facts.quote: A medium-sized bird, Pterodromoides was comparable in shape and proportions to extant petrels of the genus Pterodroma.

facts.statement: Like the snow petrel, it possessed a broad nasofrontal hinge, interorbital bridge, and fused prefrontals.
facts.quote: Similarly to the snow petrel, it has a very broad nasofrontal hinge and interorbital bridge, as well as fused prefrontals.

facts.statement: A curved and narrow impression of a salt gland is present on the skull.
facts.quote: A curved and narrow salt gland impression is present.

facts.statement: The skull features a large orbitonasal foramen and a small postorbital process located above the zygomatic process.
facts.quote: The orbitonasal foramen is large while the postorbital process is small, and located vertically above the zygomatic process.

facts.statement: Unlike Puffinus, it had a round humeral shaft without flattening.
facts.quote: Unlike Puffinus, this species has a round humeral shaft with no flattening.

facts.statement: The tarsometatarsus lacked the lateromedial compression seen in Puffinus and resembled the proportions of Cookilaria.
facts.quote: The tarsometatarsus does not exhibit the lateromedial compression seen in Puffinus, and the proportions resemble those of Cookilaria.

facts.statement: It was a seabird that hunted fish and invertebrates, likely feeding on surface prey pushed there by currents or predators.
facts.quote: Like other petrels, Pterodromoides would have been a seabird, flying out to sea in order to hunt fish and invertebrates, and it is believed to be a surface feeder which fed on prey that has been pushed towards the surface by currents or predators.

facts.statement: Evidence from North Carolina and the Mediterranean suggests it was widespread across the North Atlantic and possibly a migratory species.
facts.quote: Based on the presence of Pterodromoides remains in both North Carolina and the Mediterranean, this bird is believed to have been widespread across the North Atlantic, and possibly a migratory species with wintering grounds which included the western North Atlantic.

facts.statement: Researchers theorize that its rarity in the Yorktown Formation is due to taphonomic processes related to its surface feeding ecology.
facts.quote: It has been theorized that its rarity in the Yorktown Formation (being known from one specimen at the site) is due to taphonomic processes related to this surface feeding ecology.
